\chapter{Complexity — Subset Sum To Partition}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.NPReductions.SubsetSumToPartition
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This file states the Subset Sum and Partition decision problems over a finite type $U$
with weights in $\mathbb{N}$, and formalises the classical many-one reduction from Subset
Sum to Partition obtained by adjoining two dummy items of weights $2W - T$ and $W + T$,
where $W = \sum_{a} w(a)$ is the total weight. Completeness, soundness, and the resulting
equivalence are proved under the hypothesis $T \le W$, which is needed because
subtraction on $\mathbb{N}$ truncates at $0$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Subset Sum problem]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum}
\leanok
Given a weight function $w : U \to \mathbb{N}$ on a finite type $U$ and a target
$T \in \mathbb{N}$, the predicate asserts that some subset $S \subseteq U$ has total weight
exactly $T$, i.e.\ $\exists S,\ \sum_{a \in S} w(a) = T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partition problem]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.Partition}
\leanok
Given a weight function $v : U \to \mathbb{N}$ on a finite type $U$, the predicate asserts
that some subset $S \subseteq U$ has the same total weight as its complement, i.e.\
$\exists S,\ \sum_{b \in S} v(b) = \sum_{b \in S^{c}} v(b)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction weight function]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}
\leanok
The weight function on the augmented universe $U \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ built from a Subset
Sum instance $(w, T)$. Writing $W = \sum_{a} w(a)$, it sends the original item
$\mathrm{inl}\,a$ to $w(a)$, the first dummy item $\mathrm{inr}\,\mathsf{true}$ to
$2W - T$, and the second dummy item $\mathrm{inr}\,\mathsf{false}$ to $W + T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness of the reduction]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionCompleteness}
\leanok
\uses{SubsetSumToPartition.Partition, SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum, SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}
Let $w : U \to \mathbb{N}$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T \le \sum_{a} w(a)$. If the
Subset Sum instance $(w, T)$ has a solution, then the Partition instance with weight
function $\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}\ w\ T$ on $U \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$
has a solution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the reduction]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionSoundness}
\leanok
\uses{SubsetSumToPartition.Partition, SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum, SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}
Let $w : U \to \mathbb{N}$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T \le \sum_{a} w(a)$. If the
Partition instance with weight function
$\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}\ w\ T$ on $U \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ has a
solution, then the original Subset Sum instance $(w, T)$ has a solution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subset Sum reduces to Partition]
\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionReduction}
\leanok
\uses{SubsetSumToPartition.Partition, SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum, SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionCompleteness, SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionSoundness, SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}
For $w : U \to \mathbb{N}$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$ with $T \le \sum_{a} w(a)$, the Subset
Sum instance $(w, T)$ is solvable if and only if the Partition instance with weight
function $\lean{SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight}\ w\ T$ on $U \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$
is solvable.
\end{theorem}
